plan: - MCU with dual display support (e.g., ESP32-S3 or Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W), connected to a circular display (e.g., 1.28-inch GC9A01 LCD) and a rectangular display (e.g., 4.3-inch SPI TFT LCD) via SPI or parallel interfaces.- Integrated rotary encoder with push-button capability for main navigation, several flush-mounted tactile buttons for quick actions, and an ambient RGB LED strip for status indications.- Power managed by USB-C input with appropriate buck converters (5V and 3.3V) and a Qi2/MagSafe compatible wireless charging module for phone charging.- Optional audio components include an I2S DAC, small speaker, and an optional microphone array with a physical mute switch for voice interaction.- Custom 3D-printed curved enclosure with integrated bezels for screens, mounts for all electronic components, and a custom-designed rotary ring mechanism for tactile input.

originalPrompt:
Create a complete blueprint for a DIY futuristic desk-assistant device.

The device should be an elegant, easy-to-use desktop assistant with a graphical interface that helps me manage day-to-day life. It should show my calendar, reminders, to-do list, clock, and useful daily information. Assume calendar/reminders/tasks can be pulled from different sources such as Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, Notion, Todoist, Gmail, Telegram, or manual API/webhook inputs. Choose the best practical integration approach.

Core concept:
A small premium desk device with two screens:
1. A circular screen dedicated mostly to the clock.
2. A rectangular screen for calendar, reminders, to-do list, notifications, widgets, and daily overview.

The device should feel like a sleek futuristic assistant, not a bulky maker project. The design should be slim, curved, minimal, and modern, with a soft premium look.

Important interaction requirement:
The device must be controlled only through physical inputs. Do not use a touchscreen.

Input system:
- The circular clock display should have a physical rotary ring around it.
- The rotary ring should work as the main input method.
- The ring should allow scrolling through dashboard cards, changing modes, adjusting focus timer duration, moving through calendar items, and navigating settings.
- The rotary ring should also support press/click input if mechanically feasible, like a push-to-select control.
- Add several clean physical buttons for quick actions:
  - Back / Home
  - Confirm / Select, unless handled by the rotary ring press
  - Snooze reminder
  - Dismiss reminder
  - Start / pause focus mode
  - Optional mute/privacy button
- The buttons should be minimal and beautifully integrated into the casing, not exposed like a prototype board.
- The UX should be designed around glanceable information and fast physical control, similar to a premium smart alarm clock, car infotainment knob, or high-end audio device.

Main features to include:
- Circular clock display with analog and digital clock modes.
- Rectangular dashboard showing:
  - Today’s calendar events.
  - Upcoming reminders.
  - To-do list.
  - Weather.
  - Small daily briefing / “what’s next” section.
  - Focus timer / Pomodoro mode.
  - Notification summaries from selected sources.
  - Optional smart home status widgets.
- Button-only and rotary-ring-based navigation that is simple, intuitive, and satisfying to use.
- Ambient LED strip or subtle edge lighting for status states:
  - calm idle mode,
  - upcoming meeting,
  - urgent reminder,
  - focus mode,
  - charging mode.
- Qi2 / MagSafe-compatible magnetic charging area for a phone, integrated into the top or side of the casing if feasible.
- USB-C power input.
- Optional small speaker or buzzer for gentle reminder sounds.
- Optional microphone only if privacy is handled properly, with a physical mute switch.
- Night / low-brightness mode.
- Standby mode with beautiful clock and subtle animation.
- Local fallback mode if internet is unavailable.

Design and casing:
The casing should be skinny, curved, and futuristic. Avoid sharp boxy shapes. It should look like a premium consumer product, suitable for a clean desk setup.

The rotary ring around the circular display should be a key visual feature. It should look intentional, premium, and tactile — like a smooth metal or satin-finish control ring. It should not look like a random encoder added to a screen.

Suggested visual style:
- Main casing: matte off-white, pearl white, or soft light gray.
- Accent color: electric blue, soft cyan, mint green, or violet glow.
- Screen bezels: glossy black or dark graphite.
- Rotary ring: brushed aluminum, dark graphite, champagne metal, or satin silver.
- Shape: curved horizontal base with the circular screen slightly raised or integrated on one side, and the rectangular screen flowing next to it.
- Buttons: flush, low-profile, backlit if possible, integrated into the front edge or top curve.
- Include cable management so the power cable is hidden as much as possible.
- Make the casing 3D-printable, but make it look polished and premium.
- Suggest materials, finish, sanding/painting method, and assembly approach.

Hardware requirements:
Define the best hardware architecture from scratch. Choose appropriate boards, displays, sensors, power components, connectors, LEDs, buttons, charging module, speaker, and any other required components. Prioritize parts that are realistic to buy and assemble as a DIY project.

Please include:
- Recommended main controller/computer, such as Raspberry Pi, ESP32, or another better option.
- Exact recommended screen types and sizes for the circular and rectangular displays.
- A practical rotary ring mechanism around the circular screen.
- Recommended rotary encoder, magnetic encoder, bearing, or custom ring mechanism.
- How the rotary ring should be mounted mechanically.
- How the rotary input should connect to the controller.
- Power architecture.
- Wiring diagram description.
- Bill of materials with estimated prices.
- Alternatives for budget, balanced, and premium builds.
- Any required adapters, drivers, and mounting hardware.
- Thermal and safety considerations.

subSteps.title: 3D print all main enclosure and display bezel parts

detail.tip: Ensure your 3D printer bed is perfectly leveled for the first layers of the large enclosure parts to prevent warping.
steps: Print the Main Enclosure Bottom Shell with PETG, 25% infill, and 0.2mm layer height.
Print the Main Enclosure Top Shell with PETG, 25% infill, and 0.2mm layer height.
Print the Circular Display Bezel with PETG, 100% infill, and 0.15mm layer height.
Print the Rectangular Display Bezel with PETG, 100% infill, and 0.15mm layer height.
Carefully remove all support material and deburr edges from the printed parts.
detail.summary: 3D print all main enclosure and display bezel components.

subSteps.title: 3D print all internal mounting brackets and small mechanical components
Clean and deburr all 3D printed parts, remove supports
Test fit circular display and rectangular display into their bezels
Insert rotary encoder bearing into main enclosure top and test fit rotary ring parts
Solder power and data wires to Main Controller (ESP32-S3)
Solder power wires to Qi2/MagSafe Wireless Charging Module and USB-C Input
Solder data wires from Main Controller to Circular Clock Display and Rectangular Dashboard Display
Solder data wires for I2S Audio DAC and Microphone Module, and connect Speaker to DAC
Wire the Microphone Physical Mute Switch to the Microphone Module
Solder wires for Main Rotary Encoder and all flush buttons
Perform continuity checks on all soldered connections
Connect Main Controller to computer via USB-C and verify recognition
Upload basic test firmware to Main Controller to verify GPIO, SPI, and I2S pin assignments
Test Circular and Rectangular Displays for functionality and backlight control
Verify Rotary Encoder and all Button inputs are recognized by the Main Controller
Test I2S Audio DAC and Speaker output; verify Microphone Module input and mute switch
Test Qi2/MagSafe Wireless Charging Module's power output via USB-C port (loop-through power)
Mount the USB-C Power Input Connector into its 3D printed mount and secure in main enclosure bottom
Mount the Main Controller to the MCU mount and secure the assembly in the main enclosure bottom
Mount I2S Audio DAC, Microphone Module, Speaker, and Microphone Mute Switch with their mounts/grilles into the main enclosure bottom
Adhere Non-Slip Rubber Feet to the underside of the main enclosure bottom
Mount the Qi2/MagSafe Wireless Charging Module into its mount and secure into the main enclosure top
Install Circular and Rectangular Displays into their bezels, then adhere bezels to the main enclosure top
Mount the Rotary Encoder and all small buttons into the main enclosure top, then place their respective caps
Route and manage all internal cables using Internal Cable Clips, then close and secure the main enclosure top to the bottom

projectDescription: A desk assistant powered by an ESP32-S3, featuring a circular clock and a rectangular dashboard display. It provides interactive control via a rotary encoder and flush buttons, Qi2 wireless charging, USB-C power, and audio I/O with a physical mic mute. All housed in a sleek, 3D-printable enclosure.
